newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks drift in negative ground at midday.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks drift in negative ground at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks paused for breath at midday on Thursday, trading in negative territory as the market continued to consolidate recent gains and regroup while focusing on corporate earnings reports.

Analysts said because shares had reached such high valuations, they fell on profit-taking in the absence of fresh economic data. Earnings results set the direction of individual stocks, as investors rotated among sectors.
"The market is edgy," Dick Stein, vice president of U.S. Clearing Corp, said.
"There are a lot of people out there with nice big profits who are quick to pull the trigger," he said.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down around four points at 7840, hovering between session lows of 7809 but below intraday highs of 7888.
The Nasdaq composite slipped around five points to 1482, as the technology sector rested from its recent runup, digesting various earnings reports.
The long bond's rising yield was a slight drag on stocks, off 5/32 at to 6.58 percent.
Breadth on both the New York and Nasdaq stock exchanges was near-evenly mixed.

"Valuations have gotten so high that we need really positive news to get people buying aggressively," said Roy Blumberg, chief investment strategist at Josephthal Lyon & Ross. "A backup in bonds and some nervous after the stock market's recent volatility is enough to send shares lower."
Investors were busily rotating among groups, using results and valuations to guide their actions, traders said.
Technology stocks lost steam after some below-forecast earnings reports and after yesterday's gains, they said.

"Nasdaq has been closing at new record highs every day, so it is subject to profit-taking as the earnings come out," Jim Benning, a trader at BT Brokerage, said. "It's a question of stock selection here."
Josephthal's Blumberg said: "Techs are off but they were strong yesterday. There's a lot of rotation going on, which is typical after the market has made a large move."
Bellwether Intel Corp, a recent gainer, shed 1-7/8 to 150-3/4 in active trade, setting a softer tone for the broader technology market.

Salomon Brothers analyst Erika Klauer said she was concerned the chipmaker's second quarter earnings might fall short of expectations and she was considering reducing her third quarter earnings estimate on the company.

Compaq Computer Corp also weakened 1-1/8 to 120, after the company reported second quarter earnings of $1.48 per share, excluding a $0.73 per share charge. Results were above the First Call consensus estimate of $1.39 per share but below the so-called "whisper" estimate of $1.50.
The "whisper" number refers to unpublished earnings estimates that circulate on Wall Street ahead of earnings.
"The market cannot tolerate anything but really fantastic news," James Melcher, president of Balestra Capital said.
Other companies, like Dow component General Electric Corp, reported above-forecast quarterly results.
In the second quarter, it earned $0.66 per share, compared with $0.58 per share in the year-ago period and a First Call consensus estimate of $0.65 a share.
Its stock rose 13/16 to 69-1/4.
Kmart Corp stock lost 3/4 to 10-3/4. The retailer said markdowns in its women's apparel business would keep its second quarter net income below its year-ago profit levels.
((Wall Street desk 212-859-1730))
